contracts.title: CSM14-05 · 22 Jun 2028 — Expose an authoritative refresh preview API (180m)
contracts.implementation_task: Implement the existing Spring API adapter for a proposed POST /api/v1/shortlists/{id}/checkpoint-refresh-previews. Authorize the existing shortlist before reading its private branch metadata. Resolve at most nine exact base/local/upstream version references across three selected product slots through one public Catalog snapshot port; produce exact checkpoint/catalog generations, source digests, conflict states and a canonical preview fingerprint. The server computes this fingerprint; it is an equality aid, never authorization. A preview does not accept a branch or advance journey state.
contracts.fixture: A previews C-A/r1 and the three-slot fixture at catalog generation 20. Add one divergent local edit, one optional response metadata field, an unavailable public source and a body owner override. Foreign B requests S-A. The Catalog adapter can expose a prepared generation-change signal during snapshot capture.
acceptance: The response identifies a single declared checkpoint revision and catalog snapshot, with exact conflicts and qualified unavailable sources.
Foreign/unknown owned shortlist references use the established safe denial contract before private serialization; body owner overrides are rejected.
Preview execution leaves checkpoint head, audit/domain transition count and journey state unchanged.
A mixed catalog snapshot is rejected/retried only within the declared bounded adapter behavior; it is not presented as a coherent preview.
Additive optional metadata cannot alter required source identities or silently resolve a conflict.
contracts.architecture_evidence: Record one request/response sequence showing owner authorization, Catalog public-port access and fingerprint construction. Explain the consistency point and why a client-supplied digest or UUID is not an access credential. Bound input fan-out to three slots and at most nine exact version references; a batch boundary does not authorize any private cross-owner read.
contracts.novelty: The new API mediates a complete branch/base/upstream preview; it does not repeat the final explorer filter endpoint.

contracts.title: CSM14-06 · 23 Jun 2028 — Accept resolved refreshes with atomic revalidation (180m)
contracts.implementation_task: Implement the bounded accept-refresh application seam. Reauthorize, load the expected current head and re-read authoritative source state through public module contracts. Recompute the proposed result from the base/local intent and explicit per-conflict decisions; compare the expected generation/fingerprint. Only a fully valid, explicitly resolved plan can append a new immutable checkpoint and its required audit/journey changes. Reuse the existing transaction and lock-order mechanism so catalog publication versus acceptance has a defined order.
contracts.fixture: Preview P20 is based on C-A/r1 and catalog generation 20 with a single resolved H2 conflict. In the positive case nothing changes. In the negative case catalog advances to generation 21 before acceptance. A third case throws the prepared persistence fault between staged revision and required journey update. Unresolved/forged resolution choices are separate input cases.
acceptance: The positive case appends one exact resolved checkpoint, preserves the old revision and records only safe source/operation references.
Generation/head/fingerprint mismatch rejects without applying any resolution or changing the journey.
An unresolved conflict or a chosen version outside the authoritative allowed options cannot be accepted merely because a client calls it resolved.
Injected failure leaves domain/audit/journey state atomic; repeat uses the same durable operation identity.
A controlled publication-versus-accept schedule demonstrates the declared serialization rule; a preflight read alone is not claimed to close the race.
contracts.architecture_evidence: Save a transaction/lock-order sketch plus the observed positive/stale/rollback row sets. Explain why the comparison refresh cannot imply acceptance of quote, policy, price or insurance terms.
contracts.novelty: This is an explicit acceptance protocol for comparison metadata, with new branch reconciliation outcomes; it does not alter existing money/submit acceptance contracts.

contracts.title: CSM14-07 · 24 Jun 2028 — Render explicit branch conflicts in React (180m)
contracts.implementation_task: Implement one bounded React composition in the existing comparison screen using shared primitives and existing TanStack Query factories. Render the base/local/upstream source versions and one explicit decision control for each of at most three conflicts. Server preview lives in the query cache; unsaved choices remain local memory state tied to the preview fingerprint. The accept control submits the exact resolved plan and is disabled while unresolved, stale or unavailable.
contracts.fixture: Prepared API fixtures return one auto-resolved slot, one divergent-version conflict and one unavailable slot. Resolve the conflict, then receive a changed preview fingerprint. Exercise keyboard-only choice, loading, visible error and retry through the existing shell. No new route framework or design system is introduced.
acceptance: Visible source/version labels distinguish base, local intent and upstream proposal without implying that the proposal has already been saved.
Unresolved/unavailable/stale plans cannot invoke acceptance; tests observe zero mutation calls.
A changed preview invalidates incompatible local decisions and asks for explicit review; decisions never silently attach to another version pair.
Keyboard focus and accessible names allow selection and error recovery with the existing shared controls.
An API failure retains the unsaved draft in memory while clearly distinguishing it from the current persisted checkpoint.
contracts.architecture_evidence: Record a small state-ownership table and one executable state-transition trace. Explain which facts are authoritative server state, which are local draft intent, and how their lifetimes differ.
contracts.novelty: This new UI requires explicit three-way conflict resolution; existing saved-selection, shared-component and query-race foundations are reused.

contracts.title: CSM14-08 · 25 Jun 2028 — Recover a lost refresh acceptance response (180m)
contracts.implementation_task: Wire and test the refresh panel’s retry/reconciliation path using the existing durable command result. The server commits a resolved checkpoint but the prepared transport drops the response. The UI must show an unknown outcome, query/replay the same authorized operation identity and reconcile with the stored current checkpoint. Add the smallest adapter/state seam required; do not implement a generic offline queue or persist private mutation payloads in browser storage.
contracts.fixture: C-A/r1→r2 acceptance commits; response is suppressed. The user clicks retry while the same page retains the original operation identity. Then run a full SPA reload: authenticate and refetch the existing owned shortlist/head; do not pretend that lost in-memory unsaved choices survived. Use a prepared stale-read response to check truthful loading until authoritative refetch completes.
acceptance: Response loss does not display definite failure or trigger a new logical acceptance command automatically.
Same-operation retry returns r2 with exactly one durable revision/effect; explicit authoritative refetch settles the UI.
The reloaded SPA reconstructs the persisted r2 from authenticated server reads and states honestly that any unsaved memory-only draft was not recovered.
Stale or pending responses cannot downgrade r2 to r1 or falsely claim a new save.
No private draft/mutation cache is written to localStorage, IndexedDB or a third-party endpoint.
contracts.architecture_evidence: Retain a bounded failure/recovery sequence separating commit, delivery and observation. Explain what survives page reload and why a transport timeout is not evidence of transaction rollback.
contracts.novelty: This transfers the existing unknown-outcome principle into the newly built refresh UI/command protocol and proves its particular durable result identity.
